title: Velocity buffer and scene buffer uniform not clean at the first and second frame
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.6 rc2 ### System information Godot v4.6.beta (40f822032) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13980HX (32 threads) - 31.62 GiB memory ### Issue description This is an issue found upon implementing #115027 , we have workarounds to overpass the issue (skip motion blur effects for the first few frames) and @QbieShay suggested us to file a issue instead. The motion blur effect shows unwanted blurring at the first and second frame. Investigation shows that the problem originates from dirty data in the velocity buffer and scene buffer uniform. In the very first frame, the velocity buffer should have been empty, but in reality it is tainted and contains color values (which stands for velocities), as the image below shows: The tainting colors persist in the first and second frame. And the velocity buffer goes empty as expected starting from the third frame. At the same time, the scene data UBO should have same camera transforms for `ubo` and `prev_ubo` on the first frame. But in reality they're different, this indicates that the camera is moving before the first frame, which isn't correct. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a empty 3d scene with a cube. 2. Enable any effect that requires motion vectors (like TAA) so that motion vector rendering is on. 3. Launch the scene using renderdoc and capture the first 3 frames 4. See the velocity buffer (and also the scene buffer uniform) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Not important. Just an empty scene with a cube model will be enough.
